newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks rally 6.07 pct at close on IMF talk.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks rally 6.07 pct at close on IMF talk.

text.p: Thai stocks rallied 6.07 at the close on Wednesday as a visit to Japan by Thailand's finance minister later today raised hopes an IMF support package may be on the way for the nation's battered economy, traders said.
The SET Index roared up 38.00 points to end at 663.66. The SET 50 added 3.55 points or 7.58 percent to 50.36 in busy trade worth 9.26 billion baht.
Thai Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya and Bank of Thailand Governor Rergnchai Marakanond are due to meet their Japanese counterparts for talks this week.

Japanese officials have indicated their preparedness to provide financial assistance but appear to have made an aid package conditional on the IMF's involvement in helping manage the Thai economy, analysts said.
Hopes Thailand might allow the IMF in saw foreign investors follow an early local lead to send most blue chips close to their 10 percent daily trading ceiling, traders said.
Regional investors, especially from Taiwan, were active foreign buyers, traders said.

"The foreigners appear to have followed the locals in believing the IMF is going to be invited in. Most of our clients are waiting but volumes are probably enough to see some follow through tomorrow," said a senior trader at a European broker.
Bangkok Bank Plc added 16 baht to 181, Thai Farmers Bank Plc gained 10 to 116 and Siam Makro Plc was up 6.50 to 84.50.
